remove: The marginal teeth on the leaves. The saw-tooth edge is the busiest mark on the page, and it sits on the leaf edges nearest the col 2 text. It reads as mechanical and adds noise without adding to the engraving concept.
top_problem: The grid is nominally symmetric (64 | 328 | 32 | 328 | 64, centred on x 408), but the content does not use it. Col 2 fills 46% of its width, and the list's mass sits 23 mm left of the centred header, so the page reads as a left-set list with a centred title. The idea is also missing its boldest move: Iowa is only a 1.25 px horizontal line, so the design stays close to ref-02 panel 1 (dark ground, agave cropped lower right, tracked CANTINA) and fails the substitution test. The soil and root band should become a real Iowa ground (for example furrowed loam strata in the same engraved line) that carries as much as the rosette does.
fixes: Resolve the axis. Either set the wordmark block flush left at x 64 to match the left-weighted reading layer, or narrow col 2 to its real measure (about 176 px) and re-centre the header over the text block, which ends at 576. Do not keep a centred header over content centred at x 320.

Put every line on the 8 px baseline. Move H2 tops from 239 to 240, set description leading to 16 px, and raise the H3-to-name gap from 2 px to 6-8 px (reduce the 17 px above the H3 to keep the pitch).

Close the 56 px column-end gap to 16 px or less, or make it deliberate: end col 2's Brut Rosé on the same row as col 1's last description, or bottom-align both columns at 784. Also let the leaves occupy the 236x116 px dead field under Spirits so that it has a job.

Make the Iowa half of the idea visible. Replace the single soil line and fanned roots with an engraved loam or furrow band (parallel contour hatch in the same line family, deeper than 84 px) so that the drawing fails the substitution test against any agave bar.
Raise H3 sub-labels to 11.5 px (8.6 pt) and lighten them toward #C4B9A6 so they hold in bar light. Give H2 more contrast over the 16.5 px names through weight, not only tracking and colour.

remove: The marginal teeth (the sawtooth on every leaf edge). At actual size they read as fuzz, they add a third texture on top of the outline and the hatch, and next to col 2 they are the busiest pixels near text. Let the tapered hatch carry the anatomy.
top_problem: The typography is a stock luxury template: widely tracked Cormorant caps on dark, DM Sans tracked-caps heads and a sage botanical. The wordmark is a placeholder that does not touch the drawing, and the only Iowa idea is a hairline horizon. It fails §5's substitution test: any agave bar from Tucson to Brooklyn could print it. The boldest missing idea is to make the wordmark and the land one gesture, with the letters sitting on or cut by the soil line, or the loam/field made typographic, so that Mexico-rooted-in-Iowa lives in the type as well as the picture.
fixes: Rebuild the display wordmark so that it belongs to the engraving: drop the .34em Cormorant (82 px, 566 px wide, reads as a spa or boutique hotel) for a face with engraved or wood-type character, or letters that sit on or share the soil line, so that type and image pass word_image_integration.

Collapse the three near-identical tracked-caps sans levels. Make H2 clearly dominant (18-20 px, or set in the display face), keep H3 at 10.5 px, and set the venue sub-line in italic serif or small caps, so that the sub-line (11.5 px) is no longer bigger than H3 and does not read as a section label.

Close the dead header band and balance the page. Cut the header zone from 240 to about 190 px, and even out the columns (56 px apart): move Cognac/Brandy or set Wine's sub-heads so both columns end within 8 px.

Make the Iowa half of the thesis visible. The single hairline soil line is too weak for §5; give the loam band tonal strata or furrow texture below the line (its contrast dropped near text), so that the bottom 8% reads as Iowa soil, not as a rule.

Give the engraving true line-weight modulation. The leaves read as uniform vector monoline fans (especially the three flat left leaves); swell the hatch on the shaded flanks and thin it toward the lit edges so it stands beside ref-01's hand-made materiality instead of reading as clip art.

remove: The marginal teeth along every leaf outline: they make the silhouette fuzzy and saw-edged at arm's length, duplicate the tone the hatching already carries, and put the drawing below the clean single-weight agave line of ref-02 panel 3. Close second: the soil line where it runs alone across the empty lower-left, where it reads as a table edge, not as Iowa.
top_problem: The palette and concept are tasteful but generic, not ownable. A sage line agave on a near-black ground is the recipe of ref-02 panels 1 and 3 with the gold swapped out, and the Iowa half of the idea (the 'black loam' ground and a single hairline soil line) is invisible to a guest: the menu fails the substitution test for any mezcal bar anywhere. For a Mexican restaurant it is also chromatically cold and quiet: one desaturated accent at 5.75% gives dignity but no heat and nothing eye-catching. The boldest missing idea is a colour or structure that fuses the two places: the loam band has to read as Iowa (for example a deep, ploughed-furrow field of tone that the roots sit in, carrying the one warm accent) instead of an empty dark strip under a hairline.
fixes: Make the Iowa half legible and fill the dead lower-left: turn everything below the soil line into a distinct loam field (a slightly warmer, lighter brown with furrow texture that fades before the text), so the band has a job and the substitution test fails for other bars.

Give the palette one point of warmth that the venue earns, for example a single terracotta or chile-red used only on the H2 section heads while the drawing stays blue-green; that keeps the accent under 8% and makes the menu read as Mexican rather than as a generic moody botanical.

Style the prices so the numbers are deliberate: tabular lining figures in the name's weight 500 but in the muted ivory, or a thin space plus a small raised $-free rule, so '15' reads as a price and not a stray numeral ('Cognac VSOP 18' still reads as an age at a glance).
Remove the marginal teeth and add a clean hairline tip to every leaf, so the engraving reads at arm's length and in dim bar light like the single-stroke gold agave of ref-02 panel 3.

Raise the descriptions from 12.5 px to 13.5 px and the sub-labels from #A99F8E to #C4B9A6 (7.9 pt reversed tracked caps at 6.92:1 is the weakest text in dim light), then shorten the wordmark tracking from .34em to about .26em so the wordmark stops competing with the rosette for first focal position.

lens: design concept and art direction (15, 16) against ref-02 and the best bar menus in the country

measurements.source: render_report.json (no layout.json); CSS px at 96/in, 1 px = 0.2646 mm

margins_mm.note: The side margins are equal. Below the text, the bottom 72 mm holds the drawing, so it is the art's field, not dead canvas.

measurements.left_edges: Col 1 names all sit at x 64 and col 2 names all at x 424 (0 px spread).
measurements.price_column: Prices are inline, not in a column: the gap after every name is 15 px (constant) and travel is 5% on all 14 rows, with no row over 40%.
measurements.headers: All five H2 heads are DM Sans 600 13.5 px on the column x. All six H3 heads are 10.5 px. Every row top is a multiple of 8, and the section gap is 32 px throughout.
measurements.spacing: The item pitch is a constant 8 px.

top_problem: This is ref-02 panel 1 recoloured: a dark ground, a widely tracked CANTINA, two columns and an agave rising from the bottom-right corner. The only 'Iowa' is a single hairline that the proposal calls soil. On the page it reads as a horizon or tabletop, and the roots below it read as a reflection or light rays. The menu fails the §5 substitution test: it would work unchanged for an agave bar in Phoenix or Oaxaca. The idea it is missing is Iowa loam made visible as material: a deep stratified soil band, or furrowed prairie rows running into the vanishing point, that the agave visibly grows out of, so the fusion reads without a caption. The engraving is clean vector hatch with uniform pitch and no grain, ink spread or paper. It is competent but reads as generated line art, not the painterly or printmaking craft of the references, and a single cool blue-green on brown gives a Mexican cantina no warmth at all.
remove: The 15 radiating roots below the soil line. They read as a sunburst or water reflection, not roots, and they create a second competing horizon zone. Let a textured loam band carry the Iowa idea instead.
fixes: Make the Iowa half of the thesis legible without the proposal: turn the area below the soil line into a real loam band (stratified engraved soil or perspective furrow rows in a darker tint of the accent) that the rosette's base sinks into, so the fusion passes the substitution test.

Give the engraving materiality: vary the hatch pitch and line weight with form (swell at the leaf bellies, break near the highlights), add a subtle printmaking grain whose contrast drops to zero behind the text, and let the drawing read as an intaglio print rather than uniform vector lines.

Add one warm note justified by the concept (for example a terracotta or a loam-ochre for the H2 heads only, or a warm ivory wordmark) so the palette reads as a cantina rather than a spa or mezcaleria, keeping the accent at 8% or less.

Balance the columns: col 2 ends 14.8 mm above col 1. Either end both columns within 8 px of each other or shape the rosette so the gap reads as intentional, and pull the wordmark-to-subline gap (about 22 mm of air) tighter so the header block reads as one unit.
Raise the sub-labels from 10.5 px (7.9 pt print) to at least 11.5 px, or lift them from #A99F8E toward #C4B9A6, so tracked small caps on a dark ground stay readable in dim bar light.

lens: phone version and how print and phone hold together

measurements.source: render_report.json (no layout.json), visual_tests.json, proposal.md, preview-letter.png, preview-phone.png; compared against ref-02

letter_margins_css_px.note: The bottom is held by the art, which bleeds 12 px (3.17 mm, which passes the 3 mm bleed check). The text sits inside the 48 px safe inset.

measurements.letter_left_edges: col1 x=64 and col2 x=424. Every name shares its column edge (pass).
measurements.price_format: Inline, no $, no decimals, same size as the name (16.5 px letter, 18 px phone), muted #C4B9A6 at weight 400. It is consistent.

phone_css.dead_gap_vs_section_gap: about 2.9 times the 32 px section gap

measurements.type_level_collision: The header sub-line (DM Sans 11.5 px, tracked caps, muted) and H3 (DM Sans 10.5 px, tracked caps, muted) differ by only 1 px. They are effectively one style serving two levels.
measurements.reference_comparison: The thesis moves ref-02 panel 1 (painterly agave, cropped, on a dark ground) into line engraving, and it lands close to panel 3 (line agave on a dark field). The reading layer matches the refs' house grammar. The art does not reach their craft: the refs' leaves have gesture and tonal depth, while I5's hatch is an even, mechanical fan.

remove: The marginal teeth. The sawtooth that runs along every leaf edge reads as a zipper or clip-art serration at both letter and phone size. It is the most stamp-like device on the page, and the outline plus the cupped-margin line already carry the agave's anatomy.
top_problem: The boldest missing idea is an Iowa half that the guest can actually see. The idea does not survive the move to phone. On letter, the rosette rises beside the wine list and makes a composition. On phone, the first five screens are plain type with no gesture, and the drawing turns up only as a footer vignette after a 93 px dead gap. The roots, which are the whole Iowa half of the thesis, shrink to an 83 px sliver (4.5% of the page). On both formats, 'Iowa black loam' lives in the proposal prose: a guest sees a dark ground and one horizontal rule. The result is a well-drawn agave on a dark menu that any mezcal bar could use, so it fails the substitution test and §5's 'fuse Mexico and Iowa in the idea itself'.
fixes: Make the soil the second half of one drawing instead of a single rule. Raise the soil line so the roots and loam strata hold about a third of the art. Draw the roots with the same tapered-line grammar reaching down through the loam, cropped by the trim, so the Iowa half reads without a caption on both letter and phone.

Recompose the phone so the gesture meets the list the way it does on letter. Cut the Brut Rosé-to-leaf-tip gap from 93 px to the 32 px section gap, and let the tallest leaves rise alongside the Wine section at the right edge (clear of the text by 6 mm). Alternatively, crop a leaf tip into the first viewport under the wordmark, so the first screen is not a plain text list.

Remove the marginal teeth and rework the hatch into real engraving. Vary the pitch and swell with the form (cross-contour on the front leaves, tighter toward the heart), because the even parallel fans currently turn the front leaves into onion-like bulbs and read as generative vector fill rather than a burin.
Balance the letter column ends to within 8 px (currently 56 px, 14.8 mm). The rosette filling the shortfall under column 2 looks like a patch over the gap, not a composed interlock.

Separate the header sub-line from the H3 sub-labels, for example by setting the sub-line in the name serif at a small size or by adding clear weight and size contrast, so each level has one style. Also warm the ivory reading inks or the ground slightly, because the cool blue-green on brown currently reads spa or mezcalería rather than a lively Iowa City cantina.

lens: Every item and price checked against build/draft_doc.json (rev 3), for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: Content is intact: all 15 items and 15 prices match the draft, and nothing is invented or dropped. It still averages 77.6, below 80. Two things hold it back. First, everything outside the cocktails is thin: the spirits copy reads like a database class ('Blanco-class agave spirit · pour'). Second, the reading order moves Spirits to second place and Wine to last, which departs from the draft without a note.
problems: Prices (criterion 9): Manhattan 15, Margarita 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18 and Dry Cider 8 all match the draft exactly. That is 14 rows (the draft has 14 prices). No item is missing, invented or renamed.

Section order: the draft runs Cocktails, Beer, Wine, Spirits, Cider. Reading down column 1 and then column 2, the menu runs Cocktails, Spirits, Draft Beer, Cider, Wine. Wine now comes last, after Cider, and Spirits sit second. The proposal gives no reason or note for this. Leading with agave in a cantina can be argued for, but it has to be a stated decision, not a side effect of balancing the columns.
The draft's 'Beer' section with its 'Draft' sub-group has been merged into one 'DRAFT BEER' head. The meaning is kept, but the section name differs from the draft and the proposal does not log it.

Spirits descriptions: 'Blanco-class agave spirit · pour', 'Añejo-class agave spirit · pour' and 'Grape brandy from Cognac · pour' are taxonomy wording (NOM clase) plus a stray serve word. That fails 'guest language'. The middot before 'pour' reads like an ingredient list, not a serve.

Known data gap, not the designer's fault: the beer has no ABV, Malbec and Pinot Grigio have no region, Brut Rosé has no grape or region, and none of the spirits has a brand. Rob has been asked for these. The printed descriptions ('Crisp pale lager', 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Dry sparkling rosé') are faithful to the draft but carry almost no information, so criterion 8 stays low until the data arrives.

The Brut Rosé 13 has no pour label. It sits under 'Sparkling' and outside 'By the Glass', so a guest cannot tell whether 13 is a glass or a bottle. The proposal lists this as open, but the page does nothing to resolve it.

Tone is uneven: only the Margarita gets an italic tasting note. That is correct by the draft, but it makes one item louder than the rest. The House Daiquiri also loses the draft's word 'house' ('house demerara syrup' became 'demerara syrup'), which weakens the one House Originals signal the draft gives.

The garnishes 'lime wheel' (Margarita), 'lime coin' (Daiquiri) and 'orange peel' (Old Fashioned) are not in the draft components. They are cited to phg.recipe_versions through round-17. I accept them as sourced, but the Accuracy reviewer should confirm them against the rows. The Manhattan correctly omits aromatic bitters (public_components hides them), and its cherry garnish comes from the draft.

No taglines, side-rail text or prop captions state an item fact. The only extra text is the 'CANTINA' wordmark (a placeholder, flagged) and the sub-line '& Cocktail Bar / Iowa City, Iowa'. Both are generic.

Price format: bare integers, inline, muted #C4B9A6, about 5% eye travel, consistent across both columns. The prices associate clearly with their items. They are solid but plain: nothing distinguishes the glass tier, and the muted price ink sits close to the description ink.
fixes: Rewrite the three spirits descriptions in guest language from the known facts only, for example 'Unaged tequila, served neat' / 'Barrel-aged tequila, served neat' / 'VSOP Cognac, served neat'. Drop the '-class' wording and the '· pour' tail. Add no ages or brands until Rob supplies them.
Either restore the draft's section flow (Cocktails, Beer, Wine, Spirits, Cider) or log the reorder in the proposal as a deliberate cantina decision. In both cases Wine should come before Cider.
Give the Brut Rosé a pour label ('glass', or whatever Rob confirms), or move it under a 'By the Glass' umbrella with a Sparkling sub-label, so its 13 cannot be read as a bottle price.
Restore 'house demerara syrup' in the House Daiquiri line so the draft's house-prep claim is not dropped.

Keep the ABV, region, grape and brand gaps flagged in the proposal, and reserve a consistent slot for them in each beer and wine line (for example 'Czech-style pilsner · __% ABV'), so the data drops in without reflowing the page.

top_problem: The cocktails are well done. They list the full spirit, modifiers and garnish. The garnishes (lime wheel, lime coin, orange peel, cocktail cherry) come from recipe_versions, which the accuracy logs verify. The Manhattan's hidden aromatic bitters are correctly left off. Every other description falls short. The spirits read like database labels: 'Blanco-class agave spirit · pour' and 'Añejo-class agave spirit · pour'. The trailing '· pour' is set with the same middot as an ingredient, so it reads like one. Beer, cider and wine get only a three-word style class ('Dry red wine', 'Crisp pale lager', 'Dry sparkling cider'). Only the Margarita has a tasting note, so the menu has two voices. This is a Mexican cantina, yet the agave pours say less than the cocktails that use them.
problems: Spirits: 'Blanco-class' and 'Añejo-class' repeat the NOM class name, which is taxonomy language, not guest language. '· pour' uses the ingredient separator, so the serve word looks like an ingredient.

KNOWN DATA GAP, not the designer's fault: there is no beer ABV, no wine region, no grape for the Brut Rosé, no cider origin or ABV, and no spirit brand or añejo age. Flag missing_ingredients to Rob for all 9 non-cocktail items. It should be visible in the handoff, not silent.
Beer and wine descriptions repeat what the name already says. 'Dry-Hopped IPA' / 'Hop-forward draft IPA' echoes the name, and 'Pinot Grigio' / 'Dry white wine' adds nothing a guest does not know.

Only the Margarita gets an italic tasting note ('Bright and citrus-forward.'). The rule follows the draft, which is correct, but on the page the Margarita looks favoured and the other three cocktails look unfinished.

Reading path: column 1 runs Cocktails then Spirits, then the eye jumps up to Draft Beer, Cider and Wine in column 2. Agave spirits next to the cocktails suits a cantina, but the Cognac VSOP breaks up that agave pairing. Column 2 also ends well above column 1.
Within Classics, the draft's order (Manhattan, Margarita) is reversed to Margarita first. That is a defensible choice for the venue, but it is not recorded as a change in proposal.md.
The draft's section descriptions ('Classic and house cocktails.', 'Straight pours by category.') are dropped without a note. Dropping them is acceptable, but log it.
Housekeeping: the menu.html <title> still reads 'explore-I3 Night Field'.
Prices: all 14 match the draft exactly (15, 15, 14, 16, 7, 8, 7, 8, 12, 11, 13, 12, 16, 18). They are set inline after the name in one consistent muted style with no $, and eye travel is short.
fixes: Rewrite the spirit lines in guest language from known facts only, and move the serve word off the ingredient separator. For example: 'Blanco tequila, unaged · by the pour'. Do not add any age, brand or 100%-agave claim until Rob supplies them.

Put a visible [needs data] flag for ABV, region, grape, brand and age for every beer, cider, wine and spirit in the proposal's missing_ingredients list, so Rob's data fill can be tracked. Keep these flags off the printed page.

Either ask Rob for tasting notes for the other three cocktails, or move the Margarita's note into the same roman style as the other lines so no cocktail looks unfinished. Do not write notes that are not in the draft.
Split Spirits into Agave (placed right after Cocktails) and Brandy (placed with Wine, or last in column 2). This keeps the agave run intact and brings the column ends closer together.

In proposal.md, record the Margarita-first reorder and the dropped section descriptions as deliberate editorial changes, and fix the stale 'explore-I3' title in /home/user/phg-harmony-app/handoff/designs/test-1-iowa-city-cantina/explore-I5/menu.html.

lens: Flow and reading path for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The reading path is wrong for this venue. The letter layout is read column-first, and the phone file confirms the order, so the guest goes Cocktails, then Spirits, then Draft Beer, Cider and Wine. Spirits lands second, ahead of the everyday beer and wine that most guests order with food, which breaks the cocktails, beer, wine, spirits order. Meanwhile the agave engraving (23% of the page) pulls the eye away from the wordmark. Col 2 is laid over rising leaf tips, so there are two competing focal masses and no clear path. The design also quietly moves Margarita ahead of Manhattan within Classics, although the draft lists Manhattan first. That is a sensible lead for a cantina, but it changes the draft's order and the proposal does not note it.
problems: Section flow: Spirits sits under Cocktails in col 1, so a column-first read, and the phone build, puts it second. The scorecard order is cocktails, beer, wine, spirits. Col 2 (beer, cider, wine) is pushed to the reading end.
In Classics the order changes from the draft (Manhattan, Margarita) to Margarita, Manhattan with no note in proposal.md.

Focal order: the rosette is the largest and brightest mass on the page and rises right under col 2 (the Draft Beer and Wine rows sit beside the leaf tips), so the art competes with the menu instead of closing it. Col 1 ends at y 784 and col 2 at y 728, and the leftover space is given to the drawing rather than to reading.

Spirits descriptions use taxonomy wording ('Blanco-class agave spirit · pour', 'Añejo-class agave spirit · pour'). The trailing 'pour' reads as a stray word, not a serve label. It is sourced, but it is class-label language, not guest language.
Brut Rosé 13 under Sparkling has no glass or bottle label, so the guest cannot tell the serve. Malbec 12 and Pinot Grigio 11 rely only on the 'By the glass' sub-label.

Known data gap, not the designer's fault: beer ABV, wine region and spirit brand are missing, so beer reads 'Crisp pale lager' and wine reads 'Dry red wine'. Rob has been asked to fill them, and the proposal flags them correctly under Open items.

Venue fit on flow: nothing in the order or grouping signals a Mexican restaurant apart from the agave drawing. The agave spirits are grouped under a generic 'Spirits' head below the cocktails instead of being featured as the house category.

Price check: I verified the cocktail prices (15, 15, 14, 16) directly against build/draft_doc.json. I checked the beer, cider, wine and spirits prices against build.py's assertion and render_report price_rows, not line by line against the draft, so criterion 9 is held at 95 until that is confirmed.

Positives: inline prices (no $, travel 5%, same line on every row) keep each price tight to its item. There are no taglines or captions stating item facts. The Margarita tasting note comes from the draft. The Manhattan leaves out aromatic bitters, which is correct because the draft sets that component to hidden (public_components aromatic-bitters false).
fixes: Reorder the flow to Cocktails, then Draft Beer and Cider, then Wine, then Spirits: move Spirits to the foot of col 2 (or the phone tail) and move Beer and Cider into col 1 under Cocktails, so the column-first read follows the venue order.

Pull the rosette down and right so its tips stay below the last text row of col 2 (or at least 12 mm clear of it), so the art closes the page instead of competing with the Beer and Wine rows. Balance the column ends to within 8 px.
Either restore the draft order in Classics (Manhattan, Margarita) or record the Margarita-first swap in proposal.md as a deliberate cantina lead, for approval.

Put a clear serve label on Brut Rosé (glass or bottle, from Rob) and set the spirits serve as a label ('2 oz pour' or 'pour' in the sub-label style), not as a trailing description word. Rewrite 'Blanco-class agave spirit' as guest language from the same source (for example 'Blanco tequila, unaged').
Keep the missing ABV, wine region and spirit brand as flagged open items for Rob. Do not fill them from general knowledge.

lens: voice and consistency of descriptions, headings and venue copy; fit to a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The menu speaks in three unrelated voices and almost no Spanish. Cocktails get warm middot ingredient lists, and only the Margarita gets an italic tasting note. Beer and wine get flat class labels ('Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Hop-forward draft IPA'). The spirits read like regulation text ('Blanco-class agave spirit · pour', 'Grape brandy from Cognac · pour'), which is database wording, and 'pour' is left dangling as a noun. For a Mexican cantina, English-only headings (earlier bilingual heads 'Clásicos', 'De la Casa', 'De Barril', 'Sidra', 'Por Copa', 'Espumoso' are all dropped) plus a venue line that never says Mexican make this read as a generic dark-mode cocktail bar with an agave drawing attached.
problems: Prices: all 14 items and prices match /home/user/phg-harmony-app/handoff/designs/test-1-iowa-city-cantina/build/draft_doc.json exactly (Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18). Nothing is invented or dropped, and the Manhattan correctly hides aromatic bitters (public_components false).
There are no side-rail taglines, section-rule taglines or prop captions, so there is no item fact in brand copy. The tagline check passes.

Spirit descriptions use taxonomy language: 'Blanco-class' and 'Añejo-class' are NOM classification terms, not guest language. 'from Cognac' gives an origin to one spirit only. '· pour' repeats a serve word that the section already implies. The draft's plainer 'Blanco tequila pour' was closer to guest voice.

Beer and wine descriptions repeat the category ('Dry red wine' under a Malbec, 'draft IPA' under DRAFT BEER). This is thin because of the known data gap (ABV, region, producer, pour size are all pending with Rob), not the designer's fault, but the gap is not marked on the page or in the item copy.

Only the Margarita has an italic tasting line, so one item reads as a pet item while the other 13 have none. The rule ('only drafts that supply a note') is honest, but on the page it looks inconsistent.

Venue copy: 'CANTINA / & COCKTAIL BAR / IOWA CITY, IOWA' starts the second line with a bare ampersand. 'Cantina' is still a placeholder, and nothing says Mexican restaurant. Spanish is limited to 'Añejo' and the wordmark, even though the drawing is all Mexico.

Reading path and order: the wordmark is a clear entry point. The page then reads Cocktails, Spirits (col 1), then Draft Beer, Cider, Wine (col 2). Wine ends up last, after a one-item Cider section, and Spirits come ahead of beer and wine. Putting agave next to cocktails is defensible for this venue, but the proposal never argues it, and it departs from the draft's order.

'HOUSE ORIGINALS' holds a Daiquiri and an Old Fashioned. That is draft content, but on a Mexican-bar menu the label oversells two classics-with-a-twist. Keep the draft's grouping, but consider the heading tone.
Brut Rosé has no glass or bottle label. It sits under SPARKLING and not under BY THE GLASS, so guests cannot tell the serve (open item, correctly flagged by the designer).
Brown Butter Old Fashioned has an open dairy allergen confirmation in the draft, and the page carries no allergen cue.

Price format is consistent (inline, no $, whole numbers, muted ink, 15 px gap, 5% travel). This is correct but ordinary. Muted prices at #C4B9A6 are almost the same value as the descriptions, so price and description run together visually.
fixes: Rewrite the three spirit lines in guest voice from the same verified facts, e.g. 'Tequila blanco, unaged, served neat', 'Tequila añejo, barrel-aged, served neat' (only if the aging class is accepted as sourced) and 'Cognac VSOP, served neat'. Drop 'Blanco-class', 'Añejo-class' and the trailing '· pour'.

Restore the bilingual subheads the venue earned in earlier rounds (Clásicos · Classics, De la Casa · House Originals, De Barril · Draft, Sidra · Cider, Por Copa · By the Glass, Espumoso · Sparkling) so the language matches the Mexican concept the drawing sets up.

Give every category the same description grammar: cocktails as ingredients · garnish; beer as style · ABV; wine as grape · region; spirits as type · age. Where data is missing, leave a consistent pending slot in the data (not invented copy) until Rob supplies ABV, region, producer and brand.
Either give every cocktail a one-line italic tasting note sourced from its recipe, or drop the Margarita's note, so no single item gets a voice the others lack.

Fix the venue lines to read as one phrase (e.g. 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar · Iowa City, Iowa' or a Mexican-restaurant descriptor from the inputs), and get Rob's call on section order (Cocktails, Beer, Cider, Wine, Spirits vs. agave-next-to-cocktails) and on the Brut Rosé serve label.

lens: missing data: how the design and proposal flag the known gaps (beer ABV, wine region, spirit brand and pour, Brut Rosé glass-or-bottle label) and whether anything was invented to cover them
top_problem: Nothing is invented, and all 14 prices match build/draft_doc.json (15/15/14/16, 7/8/7, 8, 12/11/13, 12/16/18). But I5 handles the gaps by printing less and flagging vaguely. The proposal's 'Open items' is one generic line ('ABV, grape and region, and brand are still waiting on Rob'). It leaves out every pour size (beer, wine by the glass, spirits), brewery and producer, vintage, cider format, the Manhattan bitters question (needs_input 11) and the brown-butter dairy allergen on the Old Fashioned, which is a guest-safety gap and appears in no flag at all. The page also creates new problems while covering old ones. Each spirit ends in a bare '· pour' with no size, which points straight at the missing pour size and prints it as if it were content. 'Blanco-class agave spirit' is NOM taxonomy wording, not guest language, and it is vaguer than the draft's own 'Blanco tequila pour.' Brut Rosé 13 sits under a SPARKLING subhead straight after BY THE GLASS with no label, so a guest will read a price that may be a bottle price as a glass price. Beer and wine print only the draft's style lines, with no ABV and no region. Every item still has a description, but criterion 8 is not met for beer (style and ABV), wine (grape and region) or spirits (type and age), and nothing on the page or in an item-level flag list admits it.
fixes: Replace the one-line Open items with an item-by-item missing_ingredients table: all three beers (brewery, ABV, pour size), cider (producer, ABV, draft or can), Malbec and Pinot Grigio (producer, region, vintage, pour size), Brut Rosé (producer, region, glass or bottle), all three spirits (brand, age statement, pour size), Manhattan (needs_input 11, bitters display) and Brown Butter Old Fashioned (dairy allergen confirmation).

Remove the bare '· pour' from the three spirit lines until Rob supplies a pour size, and replace 'Blanco-class agave spirit' and 'Añejo-class agave spirit' with the draft's own words ('Blanco tequila' and 'Añejo tequila'), so there is no taxonomy wording and no stub that points at missing data.

Settle the Brut Rosé ambiguity: either get the glass-or-bottle answer and print it as the label, or keep 'BY THE GLASS' visibly scoped to Malbec and Pinot Grigio and leave Brut Rosé under SPARKLING with an explicit 'label pending' flag in the proposal, so a possible bottle price is never read as a glass price.

Put the dairy allergen for the brown butter-washed bourbon on the printed menu once it is confirmed, or hold the item's public copy until then; an allergen gap must not sit silently behind an 'unchanged from I4' content note.

Justify or revert the column order: col 1 goes Cocktails then Spirits and col 2 goes Beer, Cider, Wine, so a column-first reader reaches spirits second, before beer and wine. Either follow the draft's category order (Cocktails, Beer, Cider, Wine, Spirits) or state in the proposal why agave spirits sit under the cocktails for this cantina, and also note the Margarita-before-Manhattan reorder within Classics.

lens: Ingredient, garnish and label traceability; description quality; venue fit for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City; descriptions and prices laid out together
top_problem: Every printed fact traces to a source, but half the menu reads like a database. The garnishes all check out in phg.recipe_versions (log 236): Margarita 'Lime wheel' f06abb74, Manhattan 'Cocktail cherry' 9fb77eaa, House Daiquiri 'Lime coin' 14d45e57, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 'Orange peel' 7095fd3d. The cocktail ingredients match the draft_doc components, and leaving aromatic bitters off the Manhattan correctly follows public_components {'aromatic-bitters': false}. The Blanco and Añejo Tequila lines ('Blanco-class agave spirit · pour', 'Añejo-class agave spirit · pour') are the designer's paraphrase of beverage_categories node 04d72e1f 'Blanco / plata' and node 9f4dae69 'Añejo', plus the authority_note 'NOM-006-SCFI-2012 §5, clase'. Neither string appears in any source, both are exactly the taxonomy wording criterion 12 forbids, and they only repeat the item name. The same goes for 'Grape brandy from Cognac' (a88f6e79, a path reading) and for the draft-verbatim 'Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Toasty amber lager', 'Dry red wine' and 'Dry white wine'. That leaves three voices on one page: middot ingredient lists for the cocktails, category phrases for beer and wine, and taxonomy strings with a stray '· pour' for spirits. On top of that, one italic tasting note (Margarita) sits alone. The venue is a Mexican cantina, yet apart from the wordmark and the agave drawing there is no Spanish anywhere: all section heads are English, and the draft itself spells it both ways ('Tequila blanco' in the Margarita, 'Blanco Tequila' as an item name). The price relationship is good: inline, 15 px gap, 5% travel on all 14 rows, one price per row. But Brut Rosé 13 under 'Sparkling' has no glass or bottle label (the draft gives the price label ''), and the spirits' bare 'pour' names no measure.
fixes: Replace the spirits taxonomy lines with guest wording taken only from the rows: Blanco Tequila as 'Blanco / plata, poured neat or with lime' is NOT allowed ('neat' and 'lime' have no source), so use the node name 'Blanco / plata' (beverage_categories 04d72e1f), 'Añejo' (9f4dae69) and the draft's own 'VSOP Cognac pour' (draft beta cognac desc). Drop the invented '-class' / 'agave spirit' constructions, and raise missing_ingredients for tasting notes, ages and brands until Rob supplies them.

Make the cocktails appetising with sourced serve facts that are currently unused: 'over a large cube' for the Brown Butter Old Fashioned (recipe_versions 7095fd3d method), coupe for the Manhattan and Daiquiri (9fb77eaa, 14d45e57 glassware 'Coupe'), and 'house demerara syrup' for the Daiquiri (draft desc and component note 'House 1:1 demerara syrup by weight'). Then either give every cocktail one sourced italic line or drop the Margarita's lone 'Bright and citrus-forward.' so the section has one voice.

Venue fit: add correctly accented Spanish section kickers beside the English heads (Cócteles, Cerveza de barril, Sidra, Vino, Destilados / Agave), and use one word order for tequila everywhere (the draft's 'Tequila Blanco' component and the 'Blanco Tequila' item disagree; ask Rob which is the house form rather than printing both).

Beer and wine descriptions that repeat the item name ('Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Toasty amber lager', 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Dry sparkling cider') must stay marked as the known gap: list style, ABV, grape and region under missing_ingredients in proposal.md for Rob, and do not pad them with invented adjectives.

Pour labels: ask Rob for a glass or bottle label on Brut Rosé 13 and a pour size for the spirits. Until then remove the orphan trailing '· pour' from the spirit descriptions, because the 'Spirits' heading already says these are pours, and the bare word reads as a data field, not guest language.

lens: Description quality and whether the menu speaks in one guest-facing voice (criteria 10-14), with every fact checked against its source
top_problem: The menu has no single voice. It speaks in four: cocktails are middot ingredient lists; the Margarita alone gets an italic tasting note ('Bright and citrus-forward.', from draft beta_margarita); the spirits read like a classification database ('Blanco-class agave spirit · pour' and 'Añejo-class agave spirit · pour', copied from public.beverage_categories paths spirits.agave_spirits.tequila.blanco/.anejo, NOM class wording); and beer, cider and wine are two-word labels that mostly restate the name ('Dry Cider' becomes 'Dry sparkling cider', 'Brut Rosé' becomes 'Dry sparkling rosé', 'Dry-Hopped IPA' becomes 'Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Amber Lager' becomes 'Toasty amber lager', 'Malbec' becomes 'Dry red wine'). This is taxonomy wording and name repetition, the criterion-12 fail pattern. Verified facts: garnishes Lime wheel (recipe_versions f06abb74), Lime coin (14d45e57), Orange peel (7095fd3d) and Cocktail cherry (9fb77eaa) match the source (gateway log 235). Ingredient names match the draft components. Aromatic bitters is left off the Manhattan because the draft sets public_components aromatic-bitters=false, and that is correct. 'Grape brandy from Cognac' traces to beverage_categories ...grape_brandy.cognac. No invented facts and no taglines. The missing ABV, region, grape and brand data is the known gap and is not counted against this proposal.
fixes: Rewrite the three spirit lines in guest language from the same beverage_categories rows (for example 'Unaged tequila, served neat' and 'Barrel-rested tequila, served neat'), dropping '-class' and the jargon word 'pour'. Keep 'neat' only if the draft's serve word supports it; otherwise ask Rob.

Give every item the same description pattern: either one sourced sensory phrase for each item, taken from the draft, or none at all. Ask Rob for a tasting note for each item, or drop the lone Margarita italic so that one item does not speak in a different register.

Replace the beer, wine and cider lines that repeat the name with style facts the name does not already state (grape, region, style, ABV) once Rob supplies them; until then, flag each as missing_ingredients rather than printing a re-worded name.

Fit the venue: a Mexican cantina menu has no Spanish beyond 'Añejo'. It leads with one agave cocktail, has no mezcal and no Mexican lager, and pours a Czech Pilsner. Ask Rob whether the draft is final, and use Spanish in the subheads where it is correct (for example 'Clásicos' / 'De la Casa'). Ask Rob to confirm before changing section names.

Label the Brut Rosé 13 serve (glass or bottle, per the proposal's open item). Make the cocktail word order consistent: the Margarita prints 'Tequila blanco' while the spirit item is named 'Blanco Tequila', so pick one form.

lens: Venue fit for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City, IA (census ZCTA 52240/52245/52246), ingredient traceability, description voice, and how descriptions sit with prices
top_problem: The drawing says 'Mexican cantina' but the copy doesn't. Three of the 14 descriptions read like database categories rather than something a guest would say: 'Blanco-class agave spirit · pour', 'Añejo-class agave spirit · pour' and 'Grape brandy from Cognac · pour'. The beer, wine and cider lines are two- or three-word category labels ('Dry red wine', 'Hop-forward draft IPA' under a DRAFT BEER heading). No Spanish is used anywhere on purpose, so the agave engraving is the only thing that places this menu in a cantina. Verified sources (gateway log 239): garnishes come from phg.recipe_versions and all four match: Manhattan 'Cocktail cherry' (9fb77eaa), Margarita 'Lime wheel' (f06abb74), House Daiquiri 'Lime coin' (14d45e57), Brown Butter Old Fashioned 'Orange peel' (7095fd3d). Cocktail ingredients match the components in build/draft_doc.json (menu_project ddc4bb5b), and leaving aromatic bitters off the Manhattan is correct per meta.public_components. The spirit wording traces to public.beverage_categories paths tequila.blanco (name 'Blanco / plata'), tequila.anejo ('Añejo') and grape_brandy.cognac.vsop. 'Blanco-class' is the designer's paraphrase, not the source text. Nothing is invented and no tagline states an item fact, so content_integrity passes. Every price sits inline 15 px after its name (5% eye travel), so menu_item_association passes. Deductions: (1) the voice changes by section: dotted ingredient lists for cocktails, an italic tasting note on the Margarita only, taxonomy wording for spirits, fragments for beer and wine. (2) Spanish word order is inconsistent: 'Tequila blanco' in the Margarita, 'Blanco Tequila' as the spirit name. (3) Section order is Cocktails, Spirits, Beer, Cider, Wine. That gives agave its lead, but the house Daiquiri, Old Fashioned and Manhattan outweigh the one Margarita, so a Mexican cocktail bar reads as a generic American cocktail bar. (4) Brut Rosé 13 sits under 'Sparkling' as a peer of 'By the glass', so glass or bottle is ambiguous. Spirits say 'pour' with no size. Census check: 52240 (downtown) median age 28.6, 29.9% aged 21-34, median income $52,960, 11.0% Hispanic/Latino. 52245 and 52246 have 67% bachelor's-or-higher and 33-39% of households at $100k+. So $14-16 cocktails and $7-8 draft fit a grad and professional college-town crowd. The small Latino share means Spanish should be used as flavour with English beside it, not as full translation.
fixes: Rewrite the three spirit lines in guest language from the beverage_categories rows, e.g. 'Blanco / plata tequila, unaged' only if an unaged note exists on that row, otherwise 'Blanco tequila, served neat' using the draft's 'pour' as the serve, and drop the word '-class'.

Give the venue a Spanish voice where it is safe: bilingual section kickers (Cócteles / Cerveza de barril / Vino / Destilados) with the English as sub-labels, and match the source's order 'Tequila blanco' in both the cocktail and the spirit line (the item name stays as drafted).

Use one description voice for every item: either give each cocktail a short tasting line built from its components, like the Margarita's draft note, or drop the Margarita's italic note, and remove 'draft' from 'Hop-forward draft IPA' because the section head already says it.
Label Brut Rosé's serve (move it under 'By the glass' or add the draft's pour label once Rob confirms it) and add pour sizes to spirits when the draft supplies them, so no price is unlabelled.

Ask Rob to fill the known gaps (ABV and style for beer, grape and region for wine, brands for tequila and cognac), and ask whether the draft can add a Mexican lager and a mezcal, because right now only 3 of 14 items say 'Mexican'.

lens: How descriptions and prices sit together in preview-letter.png, the price-to-item gate, and whether every printed fact has a source
top_problem: The weak spot is the spirits copy. It is sourced but reads like a database: 'Blanco-class agave spirit · pour', 'Añejo-class agave spirit · pour' and 'Grape brandy from Cognac · pour' are built from the category paths in public.beverage_categories (04d72e1f blanco, 9f4dae69 anejo, a88f6e79 cognac; all proposal_status 'proposed'), and 'pour' is printed as if it were an ingredient. That is the taxonomy wording criterion 12 names as an automatic fail. The wine and beer lines are also thin: 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine' and 'Crisp pale lager' just restate the category. Both problems sit inside a menu that barely reads as a Mexican cantina: two tequilas, no mezcal, no Spanish beyond Añejo, and 'CANTINA' is still a placeholder name. What passes: all 14 prices match phg.menu_items for draft ddc4bb5b (log 233). Each price sits inline 15 px after its name (travel 5%, same line, render_report price_rows), so nothing can read as belonging to the wrong item. Every cocktail ingredient and garnish traces to the draft components or phg.recipe_versions: Margarita lime wheel f06abb74, Manhattan cocktail cherry 9fb77eaa, Daiquiri lime coin 14d45e57, Old Fashioned orange peel 7095fd3d. The Manhattan leaves out aromatic bitters correctly, because public_components sets aromatic-bitters to false. The known ABV, region and brand gap is not scored against the design. One more thing for the Content reviewer: phg.menu_items lists 'Junmai Ginjo 12', which is not in draft_doc revision 3 and is not printed.
fixes: Replace the three spirits descriptions with plain guest wording from their sources, for example 'Unaged tequila, served neat' and 'Aged tequila, served neat', using only draft or beverage_categories facts and never the words 'class' or 'agave spirit'; for Cognac VSOP drop 'Grape brandy from Cognac', which is path wording.

Take 'pour' out of the description line and set it as a small label next to the price, the way a glass or bottle label would sit (layout note for the designer), and ask Rob for Brut Rosé's serve (glass or bottle), since it sits under 'Sparkling' with an unlabelled 13.

Bring the one-line beer, cider and wine descriptions and the two-line cocktail descriptions to one voice: either give every item a short guest-language note from the draft or give none, so the Margarita's italic 'Bright and citrus-forward.' is not the only tasting note and its 3-line block does not outweigh the rest of column 1.

Make it read as a Mexican cantina using only draft data: Spanish sub-labels where the draft supports them (for example 'Agave' ahead of spirits and the 'Tequila blanco' wording), and flag missing_items to Rob for mezcal and a Mexican lager rather than inventing them.

Rethink the order, cocktails, spirits, then beer, cider and wine, with the Spirits block ending about 270 px above the soil line while column 2 runs into the art (designer note): either move agave spirits up next to cocktails on purpose as the cantina's lead, or follow the standard cocktails, beer, wine, spirits order.

lens: How descriptions and prices sit together on preview-phone.png (1170x5583), plus ingredient trace, description voice and Mexican-cantina fit for Iowa City
top_problem: The phone menu is accurate but lifeless. Four descriptions only say the item name again ('Dry-Hopped IPA / Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Amber Lager / Toasty amber lager', 'Dry Cider / Dry sparkling cider', 'Brut Rosé / Dry sparkling rosé'). The spirits print taxonomy wording ('Blanco-class agave spirit · pour', 'Añejo-class agave spirit · pour'). Criterion 12 counts both as failures. Apart from the agave drawing and the word 'Añejo', nothing on the page reads as a Mexican cantina: no Spanish voice, no mezcal, and 'CANTINA' is still a placeholder.
verified: Margarita garnish 'Lime wheel', glass Rocks: phg.recipe_versions f06abb74 (gateway log 237).
House Daiquiri garnish 'Lime coin', glass Coupe: phg.recipe_versions 14d45e57.
Brown Butter Old Fashioned garnish 'Orange peel', glass Rocks: phg.recipe_versions 7095fd3d.
Manhattan garnish 'Cocktail cherry', glass Coupe: phg.recipe_versions 9fb77eaa. Aromatic bitters are hidden by the draft's meta.public_components, so leaving them off is correct.
Blanco Tequila: public.beverage_categories spirits.agave_spirits.tequila.blanco, name 'Blanco / plata'.
Cognac VSOP: public.beverage_categories spirits.brandy_fruit_spirits.grape_brandy.cognac.vsop, name 'VSOP'. The menu prints no age statement, which is correct.
'pour' and the Margarita note 'Bright and citrus-forward.' both come from build/draft_doc.json.
Beer, cider and wine descriptions are the draft's desc text word for word.
All 14 prices match the draft (build.py asserts them). The render report's price_rows show every price on the same line as its name, 16 px gap, 5% eye travel.
problems: Criterion 12: descriptions that repeat the name. 'Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Toasty amber lager', 'Dry sparkling cider' and 'Dry sparkling rosé' only restate their item names. 'Dry red wine' and 'Dry white wine' say nothing a guest does not already know from 'Malbec' and 'Pinot Grigio'. The source is the draft, but the result still fails the guest.

Criterion 12: taxonomy wording. 'Blanco-class agave spirit' and 'Añejo-class agave spirit' come straight from the beverage_categories class labels and the NOM 'clase' wording. That is database language, not guest language, and the scorecard names it as an automatic-fail pattern.

Criterion 12: two voices. The cocktails are lowercase ingredient lists joined by middots. Beer, wine and cider are adjective phrases. Only the Margarita gets an italic tasting note, so on the phone it looks like a stray line rather than a system.

Criterion 13: the menu could belong to any American cocktail bar. There is no Spanish voice (section heads, kickers or sub-labels), no mezcal or agave depth beyond two tequilas, and no Mexican beer. The beer is a Czech Pilsner, an IPA and an amber lager. 'CANTINA' is still the placeholder venue word. The drawing carries the whole Mexico-meets-Iowa idea by itself.

Criterion 14 (phone): 'Brut Rosé 13' sits under a 'Sparkling' label with no pour label, so glass or bottle is ambiguous. Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP each end in '· pour' tacked onto the description instead of a consistent serve label.

Criterion 14 (phone): content ends at about 1277 css px and the art starts at 1301, but the lower third of the phone page is the drawing, with an empty band above it. On a phone the guest scrolls through a long stretch of art after the last price, and the Wine section looks cut off rather than finished.

Criterion 14 (phone): each price is the same size (16.5 px) as its name and only a little less bright. Next to the 12.5 px descriptions, a 1- or 2-digit price after a short name like 'Malbec 12' or 'Dry Cider 8' reads as part of the name, not as a price.
